scope: Six pretrained encoders plus three seed-matched random AnyPPG encoders; Native-Ridge, PCA16-Ridge, PCA16-MLP; hand features with same heads, small CNN, train mean; four fixed PPG respiratory modulation methods.
primary_result: No one of the 21 prespecified model-vs-CNN / pretrained-Any-vs-random comparisons passes Holm correction within target at 0.05.
respiration_interpretation: Train-only patient mean MAE is 2.3884 breaths/min, below all controlled MLP foundation-model means. Current evidence does not establish useful respiratory information beyond this constant baseline.
respiration_interface_limit: The common protocol averages four 8-second embeddings over 32 seconds. It preserves observation coverage but discards ordering and cross-piece respiratory modulation. This is a test of this frozen representation/aggregation interface, not an architecture-wide impossibility result.
blood_pressure_interpretation: Some point estimates are better than the small CNN, but intervals/multiplicity do not support a universal gain; handcrafted morphology is competitive. The official BP target is reproducible from ABP peaks/troughs, but inputs are clinical finger PPG and all selected patients come from MIMIC.
cohort: PulseDB uses 100 training,20 validation,42 unseen CalFree test patients; 50 segments/person; 242 AAMI patients and four pilot-exposed test patients excluded. Bounded 50000-row local-availability search found only42 of the requested maximum50 eligible CalFree patients.
pretraining_exposure: AnyPPG pretraining includes PulseDB and other encoder source cohorts may overlap; downstream split disjointness does not prove unseen-at-pretraining patients.
traditional_methods: All four respiratory variants are reported. Median fusion was fixed as the primary conventional method before formal learned comparisons; the lower observed baseline-modulation error was not used for post hoc model selection.
reference_audit: All735 BIDMC rows and8100 PulseDB rows independently reread. Model audit reloaded606 outputs;18 real-data Ridge checks used float64 matching production sufficient-statistics precision. Initial audit with sklearn preserving float32 showed conditioning error, so only independent verification precision was corrected; trained models and predictions were unchanged.
SpO2: Removed from new formal training and performance comparison. Historical replication and pilot results preserved.
